Triage: lands in `packages/spec` ⇒ **`domain:spec`**; **type `Bug`, `priority:p2`, `pm:blocked`.**

## `pm:blocked`, and the block is live — measured 2026-09-10T17:21:00Z

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| PR #17486 | **open, `draft=true`, `mergeable_state=blocked`** — not merged |
| #15942 | **open**, `pm:dispatched` to `os-justin`, `priority:p1`, `security`, `needs:contract-review` |

⇒ All three prescriptions are **TRUE today** — the runtime confirmation door has not shipped. They become false the moment #17486 merges. ⛔ Correcting them now would make the published text wrong in the other direction, and in the more dangerous direction: it would promise a pause that does not yet exist.

`Blocked-by: #15942` recorded on the body — the **issue**, not the PR, so the unlock scan can fire when it closes.

## ⭐ Why p2 rather than p3, unlike the other two docs-drift cards this fire

The other two mislead about a shape. This one will mislead about a **safety gate**, and the card names the direction precisely:

> they tell an author the safety flag stops nothing, so an author who reads them concludes the gate is inert and arranges a human in the loop some other way, or stops setting the flag at all.

⇒ An author who stops setting `requiresConfirmation` because the prose says it is inert **loses the gate** at the moment it starts working. And these are not comments — the first reaches consumers as a **parse-error prescription on a `.strict()` schema**, and the other two are what `spec-changes.json`, the upgrade guide and `os migrate meta` project. ⇒ Shipped text on a security-adjacent surface.

⭐ The card's own framing is the sharpest statement of the class and I am keeping it: #15942 was 「published prose promises a pause the runtime does not perform」; this is 「published prose denies a pause the runtime now performs」. **Same class, same surface, opposite sign.**

⚠️ ⛔ Not p1: nothing is wrong today, and #15942 — the p1 with `security` — is the card that carries the real exposure. This one is its residue and cannot bite until that one lands.

## On release

⚠️ Re-verify the three sites still read as quoted **on the merged ref** before dispatching — #17486 is a draft and its own diff may already correct one or more of them. ⇒ The card's premise is 「PR #17486 makes all three false」, and a dev must falsify that per-site rather than assume all three survive.

The card carried it when I read it live (my cached board copy showed no labels, which is why the removal was not in the write). ⇒ A grade and a `finding` on one card is a half-state, and it would have kept this card in the ungraded-finding sweep after it was graded.
